subsystems.name: Bioluminescence gene cassette
subsystems.role: the added DNA that makes the plant produce light.

subsystems.name: Substrate supply
subsystems.role: the glow needs a starting chemical, which comes from the plant's own metabolism.
parts: caffeic acid from the phenylpropanoid pathway
enzymes that divert it toward hispidin

subsystems.name: Host plant line
subsystems.role: the organism the genes are put into, and where they are switched on.

subsystems.name: Transformation and regeneration pipeline
subsystems.role: the laboratory process that turns a single engineered cell into a whole plant.

subsystems.name: Containment and regulation
subsystems.role: keeping the trait controlled and legal to sell.

buildSteps.title: Choose and synthesise the pathway genes
buildSteps.detail: Genes for the fungal light pathway — a hispidin synthase, a hydroxylase and the Luz luciferase — are chemically synthesised, with codons rewritten to suit the plant.

buildSteps.title: Attach plant control elements
buildSteps.detail: Each gene is paired with a promoter and terminator so it is expressed strongly in leaves and stems rather than only in roots or seeds.

buildSteps.title: Insert the DNA into plant cells
buildSteps.detail: Leaf discs or callus tissue are co-cultured with Agrobacterium carrying the cassette, which transfers the DNA into the plant genome.

buildSteps.title: Select and regenerate
buildSteps.detail: Successfully transformed cells are grown out with a selection marker and coaxed through tissue culture until they form shoots, then whole rooted plants.

buildSteps.title: Screen and brighten
buildSteps.detail: Plants are grown and imaged in the dark; the brightest are kept, and the enzymes and promoter strengths are adjusted to push more of the plant's caffeic acid down the light-producing route.

buildSteps.title: Stabilise and multiply
buildSteps.detail: Chosen lines are self-pollinated and grown on to confirm the trait is inherited reliably and the glow lasts through the plant's life.

buildSteps.title: Review and release
buildSteps.detail: Regulators assess the plant for environmental and food safety, after which it can be propagated in a greenhouse and sold as an ornamental.

prerequisites.why: without a working tissue-culture route from single cell to whole plant, no engineered houseplant is possible.
the genes and the hispidin chemistry had to be mapped before they could be moved into a plant.

prerequisites.tech: Metabolic engineering of the host's phenylpropanoid pathway
prerequisites.why: the glow is limited by how much caffeic acid the plant can spare, and boosting that flux is not yet routine.

prerequisites.tech: Robust regulatory framework for ornamental GMOs
prerequisites.why: approval is country-by-country, so the same plant can be legal in one market and not another.

prerequisites.tech: Light output comparable to room lighting
prerequisites.why: current glow is faint and best seen in a dark room, and photosynthesis caps how much energy a plant can invest in making light.

pathway.milestone: a genetically engineered glowing petunia was cleared for sale in the United States in 2023 and reached home growers, with earlier glowing tobacco plants demonstrated in 2020 research
pathway.unlocks: the first consumer ornament that produces its own visible light.

pathway.milestone: brighter lines and more species, with different colours from variant luciferases
pathway.unlocks: glowing garden and indoor plants that are genuinely decorative rather than novelty.

pathway.milestone: rewired plant metabolism that sends far more carbon into the light pathway
pathway.unlocks: a glow visible in a lit room, opening up use as dim ambient lighting.

pathway.milestone: engineered trees or landscape planting used as night-time lighting
pathway.unlocks: street and park lighting with no electricity supply — plausible only if the energy budget can be made to work at all.
